Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 1, verse 1:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Fatiha (the Opening), because it occurs at the beginning of the Noble Qur'an; the Mushaf opens with it in writing and recitation, and it is recited at the beginning of the prayers and other occasions.

From the objectives of the surah

• Praising Allah with all kinds of praise, affirming His Lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah), singling Him out for divinity and for worship in all its forms, believing in Allah's names and attributes, and affirming the Resurrection and recompense.

• Turning to Allah, the Exalted, seeking guidance to the true religion and the straight path, seeking success and steadfastness in faith, following the way of the righteous, and avoiding the path of those who have earned anger and those who are astray.

[Tafsir]

I begin the recitation of the Qur'an with the name of Allah, seeking His help. ﴿Allah﴾ is a proper name for the Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, the one truly worshipped without any other, and it is the most specific of Allah's names; no one other than Him is named by it, glory be to Him. ﴿al-Rahman﴾ the One of universal mercy, whose mercy encompasses all creation; ﴿al-Rahim﴾ the One of mercy toward the believers. They are two of His names, containing the affirmation of the attribute of mercy for Allah, as befits His majesty.

Praise belongs to Allah, through His attributes, all of which are attributes of perfection, and through His blessings, both apparent and hidden, religious and worldly. Implicit in this is a command to His servants to praise Him, for He alone deserves it. He, glorified is He, is the Originator of creation, the One who sustains their affairs, and the Nourisher of all His creatures through His blessings, and of His allies (awliya') through faith and righteous deeds.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 1, verse 3:

﴿Al-Rahman (the Most Gracious)﴾, the One of general mercy whose mercy encompasses all creation; ﴿al-Rahim (the Most Merciful)﴾, toward the believers. Both are two of the names of God, exalted is He.

He alone, glory be to Him, is the Owner of the Day of Judgment, and it is the Day of Recompense for deeds. In the Muslim's recitation of this verse in every rak'ah of his prayers, there is a reminder to him of the Last Day and an exhortation to prepare for it through righteous deeds and to refrain from sins and evil acts.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 1, verse 5:

"You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help in all our affairs. So the matter entirely rests in Your hand; no one possesses from it even an atom's weight. In this verse is evidence that a servant may not direct any kind of worship, such as supplication, seeking aid (istighathah), sacrificial slaughter, and circumambulation (tawaf), except to Allah alone. And in it is the healing of hearts from the disease of attachment to other than Allah, and from the ailments of showing off (riya'), self-admiration ('ujb), and arrogance (kibriya')."

Guide us and show us the way; grant us success in following the straight path, and keep us firm upon it until we meet You. It is Islam, the clear path that leads to the pleasure of Allah and to His Paradise, to which the Seal of His messengers and prophets, Muhammad (ﷺ), pointed. There is no way for the servant to attain happiness except by remaining steadfast upon it.

The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, of the prophets, the truthful ones (al-siddiqeen), the martyrs, and the righteous. They are the people of guidance and steadfastness. And do not make us of those who took the path of those who earned Your anger, who knew the truth but did not act upon it, and they are the Jews, and whoever is of their kind. And do not make us of those who are astray, and they are those who did not find guidance out of ignorance on their part, and so they lost the way, and they are the Christians, and whoever follows their way.

In this supplication is a healing for the heart of the Muslim from the disease of denial, ignorance, and misguidance, and an indication that the greatest blessing of all is the blessing of Islam. Whoever knows the truth better and follows it is more entitled to the straight path. There is no doubt that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are the most entitled of people to this, after the prophets, peace be upon them. So the verse indicates their virtue and their great rank, may Allah be pleased with them. It is recommended for the reciter to say in the prayer, after reciting al-Fatihah: "Amin" (آمين), and its meaning is: "O Allah, answer." It is not a verse of Surat al-Fatihah by the consensus of the scholars; for this reason they agreed on not writing it in the copies of the Qur'an.
